title: Erosion Attack for Adversarial Training to Enhance Semantic Segmentation Robustness
abstract: Existing segmentation models exhibit significant vulnerability to adversarial attacks. To improve robustness, adversarial training incorporates adversarial examples into model training. However, existing attack methods consider only global semantic information and ignore contextual semantic relationships within the samples, limiting the effectiveness of adversarial training. To address this issue, we propose EroSeg-AT, a vulnerability-aware adversarial training framework that leverages EroSeg to generate adversarial examples. EroSeg first selects sensitive pixels based on pixel-level confidence and then progressively propagates perturbations to higher-confidence pixels, effectively disrupting the semantic consistency of the samples. Experimental results show that, compared to existing methods, our approach significantly improves attack effectiveness and enhances model robustness under adversarial training.

title: Causally structure constrained boundary generative modeling for imbalanced anomaly classification in railway signaling equipment
abstract: Abstract To address the challenges of severe class imbalance and insufficient causally structure constrained boundary in railway signaling equipment anomaly classification, this paper proposes a novel anomaly classification method that integrates causal structural constraints with boundary enhancement. First, abnormal textual records from railway signaling equipment are preprocessed through data cleaning and tokenization, and global semantic features are extracted using a RoBERTa-based encoder. Subsequently, a boundary sampling causal structure constrained generative adversarial network (BSCGAN) is introduced to perform data augmentation by explicitly modeling causal relationships among anomaly entities. This mechanism enhances feature representation for minority classes while preserving semantic consistency and causal plausibility. Moreover, targeted sampling around decision boundaries enables the generated instances to better capture latent structural dependencies between anomaly entities, thereby improving discriminative performance under complex class distributions. During feature learning, the balanced semantic representations are simultaneously fed into two parallel branches, namely an anomaly classification branch and a text generation branch. In the anomaly classification branch, a BiLSTM network is employed to model contextual dependencies, while a multi-head attention mechanism adaptively emphasizes critical semantic features, enabling effective fusion of global context and local discriminative cues. In parallel, the generative branch reconstructs abnormal textual representations under causal structural guidance. Experimental results on real abnormal textual data collected from a railway signaling maintenance division demonstrate that the proposed method achieves precision, recall, and F 1-score of 95.92%, 95.08%, and 95.50%, respectively, outperforming several competitive baselines. These findings confirm the effectiveness and interpretability of the causal structure constraint boundary generation mechanism and the learning strategy for modeling minority classes and classifying anomalies. The proposed method demonstrates practical potential in anomaly classification of railway signal equipment.

title: A Dual Perspective on Synthetic Trajectory Generators: Utility Framework and Privacy Vulnerabilities
abstract: Human mobility data are used in numerous applications, ranging from public health to urban planning. Human mobility is inherently sensitive, as it can contain information such as religious beliefs and political affiliations. Historically, it has been proposed to modify the information using techniques such as aggregation, obfuscation, or noise addition, to adequately protect privacy and eliminate concerns. As these methods come at a great cost in utility, new methods leveraging development in generative models, were introduced. The extent to which such methods answer the privacy-utility trade-off remains an open problem. In this paper, we introduced a first step towards solving it, by the introduction and application of a new framework for utility evaluation. Furthermore, we provide evidence that privacy evaluation remains a great challenge to consider and that it should be tackled through adversarial evaluation in accordance with the current EU regulation. We propose a new membership inference attack against a subcategory of generative models, even though this subcategory was deemed private due to its resistance over the trajectory user-linking problem.

title: When Can We Trust Deep Neural Networks? Towards Reliable Industrial Deployment with an Interpretability Guide
abstract: The deployment of AI systems in safety-critical domains, such as industrial defect inspection, autonomous driving, and medical diagnosis, is severely hampered by their lack of reliability. A single undetected erroneous prediction can lead to catastrophic outcomes. Unfortunately, there is often no alternative but to place trust in the outputs of a trained AI system, which operates without an internal safeguard to flag unreliable predictions, even in cases of high accuracy. We propose a post-hoc explanation-based indicator to detect false negatives in binary defect detection networks. To our knowledge, this is the first method to proactively identify potentially erroneous network outputs. Our core idea leverages the difference between class-specific discriminative heatmaps and class-agnostic ones. We compute the difference in their intersection over union (IoU) as a reliability score. An adversarial enhancement method is further introduced to amplify this disparity. Evaluations on two industrial defect detection benchmarks show our method effectively identifies false negatives. With adversarial enhancement, it achieves 100\% recall, albeit with a trade-off for true negatives. Our work thus advocates for a new and trustworthy deployment paradigm: data-model-explanation-output, moving beyond conventional end-to-end systems to provide critical support for reliable AI in real-world applications.

title: Toward Clinically Acceptable Chest X-ray Report Generation: A Qualitative Retrospective Pilot Study of CXRMate-2
abstract: Chest X-ray (CXR) radiology report generation (RRG) models have shown rapid progress, yet their clinical utility remains uncertain due to limited evaluation by radiologists. We present CXRMate-2, a state-of-the-art CXR RRG model that integrates structured multimodal conditioning and reinforcement learning with a composite reward for semantic alignment with radiologist reports. Across the MIMIC-CXR, CheXpert Plus, and ReXgradient datasets, CXRMate-2 achieves statistically significant improvements over strong benchmarks, including gains of 11.2% and 24.4% in GREEN and RadGraph-XL, respectively, on MIMIC-CXR relative to MedGemma 1.5 (4B). To directly compare CXRMate-2 against radiologist reporting, we conduct a blinded, randomised qualitative retrospective evaluation. Three consultant radiologists compare generated and radiologist reports across 120 studies from the MIMIC-CXR test set. Generated reports were deemed acceptable (defined as preferred or rated equally to radiologist reports) in 45% of ratings, with no statistically significant difference in preference rates between radiologist reports and acceptable generated reports for seven of the eight analysed findings. Preference for radiologist reports was driven primarily by higher recall, while generated reports were often preferred for readability. Together, these results suggest a credible pathway to clinically acceptable CXR RRG. Improvements in recall, alongside better detection of subtle findings (e.g., pulmonary congestion), are likely sufficient to achieve non-inferiority to radiologist reporting. With these targeted advances, CXR RRG systems may be ready for prospective evaluation in assistive roles within radiologist-led workflows.

title: Sharpness-Aware Minimization with Z-Score Gradient Filtering
abstract: Deep neural networks achieve high performance across many domains but can still face challenges in generalization when optimization is influenced by small or noisy gradient components. Sharpness-Aware Minimization improves generalization by perturbing parameters toward directions of high curvature, but it uses the entire gradient vector, which means that small or noisy components may affect the ascent step and cause the optimizer to miss optimal solutions. We propose Z-Score Filtered Sharpness-Aware Minimization, which applies Z-score based filtering to gradients in each layer. Instead of using all gradient components, a mask is constructed to retain only the top percentile with the largest absolute Z-scores. The percentile threshold Qpdetermines how many components are kept, so that the ascent step focuses on directions that stand out most compared to the average of the layer. This selective perturbation refines the search toward flatter minima while reducing the influence of less significant gradients.

title: DiffusionCom: Structure-Aware Multimodal Diffusion Model for Multimodal Knowledge Graph Completion
abstract: Multimodal knowledge graphs (MKGs) are widely used in recommendation systems, information retrieval, and question answering, but they remain highly incomplete, driving the need for multimodal knowledge graph completion (MKGC) methods. Most existing approaches rely on discriminative models that maximize conditional likelihood, neglecting the underlying data distribution and limiting their ability to capture complex real-world relations. To address this, we propose DiffusionCom, a structure-aware multimodal diffusion model for MKGC. DiffusionCom frames MKGC as generating the joint probability distribution of (head, relation) pairs and candidate tail entities from noise. We also propose Structure-MKGformer as its encoder, which captures structural information via a multi-modal graph attention network (MGAT) and adaptively fuses it with entity representations. Trained with both generative and discriminative losses, DiffusionCom outperforms state-of-the-art models on FB15k-237-IMG and WN18-IMG datasets—notably, achieving a 27.5% relative improvement in Hits@1 on FB15k-237-IMG.

title: Neuroevolution of Liquid State Machine Based on Neural Configurations and Positions
abstract: Liquid State Machines (LSMs), a reservoir computing model based on recurrent spiking neural networks, provide a powerful framework for solving spatiotemporal classification tasks by leveraging rich temporal dynamics and event-driven processing. Although the traditional LSM formulation assumes a fixed, randomly generated reservoir, recent research has explored optimization strategies to improve liquid dynamics. However, most existing approaches focus primarily on optimizing synaptic connectivity or reservoir structure, while the role of neuron-level parameters remains largely underexplored. This work proposes a neuroevolutionary strategy based on a Genetic Algorithm (GA) that encodes both neuron configurations and their spatial positions, explicitly treating neuron-level parameters as optimization targets. By evolving neuron-specific parameters and spatial positions, the method induces diverse reservoir dynamics. Unlike approaches that directly optimize synaptic weights, the proposed representation maintains an encoding whose dimensionality scales linearly with the number of neurons. The approach was evaluated on four synthetic benchmark tasks, including one Frequency Recognition task and three Pattern Recognition tasks, using compact reservoirs composed of only 20 Leaky Integrate-and-Fire neurons. Despite the small reservoir size, the method achieved state-of-the-art or highly competitive performance, reaching mean accuracies of up to 99.71%. In the most challenging case (PR12), performance improved when the reservoir size was increased to 64 neurons. The method was further evaluated on two real-world datasets, N-MNIST and the Free Spoken Digit Dataset (FSDD), using reservoirs of 300 neurons, achieving 90.65% and 81.47% accuracy, respectively, while using substantially fewer neurons than many existing LSM-based approaches. These results highlight the potential of evolving neuron configurations and spatial organization to produce compact and effective liquid reservoirs.

title: Detection of Thyroid Cancer using GoogLeNet
abstract: Thyroid cancer is one of the fast-growing cancers in the world. The cases are rising more rapidly and for this faster and accurate diagnosis should require. Computed Tomography (CT) images are very crucial for detecting the Thyroid cancer. interpreting CT images by hand takes a lot of time and can vary between observers. To overcome these issues, this paper shows the implementation of deep learning framework for detection of thyroid cancer using a fine-tuned GoogleNet. The thyroid CT image Dataset which is used in this study is taken from the Kaggle [14], the dataset is splitted into 70% for training the model, 15% for testing, and 15% for validation. The GoogleNet is trained with Artificial Bee Colony Optimizer (ABC), Ant Colony Optimizer (ACO) and Adam Optimizer. After training this optimizer by comparing the parameters, the Adam optimizer classified the Thyroid images more efficiently and got 0.99 Accuracy. This can help in early detection of thyroid cancer in real world applications.

title: Octopus: Enhancing Distributional Reinforcement Learning Through Regularization
abstract: Distributional reinforcement learning (RL), which models the full distribution of future returns rather than just the expected value, has achieved significant progress in recent years. Concurrently, regularization techniques have proven highly effective in enhancing the stability and generalization of RL agents. However, the interplay between these two paradigms remains largely unexplored. In this work, we introduce Octopus, a novel reinforcement learning framework that unifies distributional RL with regularized RL. Our theoretical results provide guarantees for both policy evaluation and control, offering insights into the benefits of regularization within the distributional RL setting. Empirically, Octopus consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on the Arcade Learning Environment, achieving superior performance. These findings highlight the robustness and practical viability of Octopus, laying a solid foundation for its application in real-world reinforcement learning tasks.

title: Cross Paraphrastic Invariance Learning for Hallucination Detection
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) frequently generate hallucinations, which are unsupported by a source document. To avoid costly LLM-as-evaluator pipelines and the heavy annotation demands of existing classifiers, we propose CPIL (Cross Paraphrastic Invariance Learning), a two-stage Siamese framework that maximizes the utility of existing labeled data. Concretely, CPIL constructs informative training pairs by: (i) generating paraphrastic views of each document-claim example as positives, and explicitly aligning their representations to enforce invariance to surface form; and (ii) mining same-document, opposite-label pairs as hard negatives to sharpen document-sensitive decision boundaries. Then CPIL conduct a two-stage model training: Stage 1 performs contrastive pretraining to learn a paraphrase-invariant, grounding-aware embedding space; and Stage 2 attaches a lightweight classifier for binary groundedness. On the LLM-AggreFact benchmark (11 tasks), CPIL surpasses strong baselines concerning F1 scores with only ~ 1% labeled data, showing its prediction superiority and label efficiency.

title: DebiasHSD: Failure-Guided Debiasing for Cross-Domain Hate Speech Detection
abstract: Hate speech detection is vital for curbing online abuse, yet current systems often fail to generalize across domains due to biases such as identity-related terms that induce spurious correlations. Existing methods attempt to reduce these biases but typically rely on costly auxiliary data or predefined cues, limiting scalability. We propose DebiasHSD, a failure-guided de-biasing framework that improves cross-domain generalization without extra bias labels. DebiasHSD trains two complementary models: a biased model that intentionally overfits to spurious shortcuts to act as a bias detector, and a debiased model that learns invariant features by focusing on cases where the biased model fails. Moreover, a bias-guided data augmentation module further supports both models by generating synthetic examples aligned with their learning objectives. Extensive experiments on four real-world benchmarks show that DebiasHSD consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches, delivering strong cross-domain generalization.

title: ALFM: Adaptive Local Feature Mining of Vision-Language Models for Out-of-Distribution Detection
abstract: Out-of-distribution (OOD) detection is crucial for the robustness of machine learning in open-world scenarios. Most existing zero-shot OOD detection methods rely on the matching similarity between global visual features and in-distribution (ID) class prompts, and exhibit limited utilization of local features. To address this, we propose a post-hoc method—Adaptive Local Feature Mining(ALFM), which dynamically provides more critical local information to help distinguish ID samples from OOD samples. Experiments on the large-scale ImageNet-1K OOD benchmark demonstrate that ALFM can not only improve the hit rate of key local patches, but also effectively enhance OOD performance under both the zero-shot and few-shot settings.

title: SPOC: Safety-Aware Planning Under Partial Observability and Physical Constraints
abstract: Embodied Task Planning with large language models faces safety challenges in real-world environments, where partial observability and physical constraints must be respected. Existing benchmarks often overlook these critical factors, limiting their ability to evaluate both feasibility and safety. We introduce SPOC, a benchmark for safety-aware embodied task planning, which integrates strict partial observability, physical constraints, step-by-step planning, and goal-condition–based evaluation. Covering diverse house-hold hazards such as fire, fluid, injury, object damage, and pollution, SPOC enables rigorous assessment through both state and constraint-based online metrics. Experiments with state-of-the-art LLMs reveal that current models struggle to ensure safety-aware planning, particularly under implicit constraints. Code and dataset are available at https://github.com/khm159/SPOC.

title: ProRank: Progressive Context Refinement for Reliable Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: The quality of retrieved context is a critical bottleneck for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems, as existing refinement methods often provide noisy or irrelevant information. Current approaches are typically limited to single-metric, document-level filtering or risk degrading the generator’s capabilities through coupled end-to-end fine-tuning. To address this, we introduce ProRank, a progressive two-stage pipeline that uses a fine-tuned, multidimensional LLM reranker for document-level selection, followed by fine-grained intra-document refinement to construct a highly information-dense context. This decoupled approach preserves the generator’s integrity while achieving state-of-the-art performance on knowledge-intensive benchmarks.

title: CoETR 2 : Complementary Packet-Based Modeling for Encrypted Traffic
abstract: The increasing adoption of modern encryption protocols has reduced plaintext availability in network traffic, posing challenges for encrypted traffic classification (ETC). Recent image-based ETC methods suffer from semantic misalignment, where packet bytes from unrelated protocol fields become spatially adjacent in the image layout, misleading spatial embedding. To address this issue, we propose CoETR2, a novel traffic representation framework that treats each complete packet, rather than individual bytes, as the fundamental modeling unit. To extract complementary packet-level features, two specialized modules are introduced: Packet Temporal Module, which captures temporal dependencies among packets, and Packet Clustering Module, which applies a refined clustering algorithm to discover temporally distant yet semantically correlated packets, yielding features that complement temporal-based features. A customized packet-based embedding is also designed to preserve packet semantics while maintaining compatibility with both modules. Experiments on four public and one private datasets demonstrate that CoETR2outperforms existing methods across diverse scenarios.

title: Chain of Correction for Full-Text Speech Recognition with Large Language Models
abstract: Full-text error correction with Large Language Models (LLMs) for Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) is attracting increased attention for its ability to address a wide range of error types, such as punctuation restoration and inverse text normalization, across long context. However, challenges remain regarding stability, controllability, completeness, and fluency. To mitigate these issues, this paper proposes the Chain of Correction (CoC), which uses a multi-turn chat format to correct errors segment by segment, guided by pre-recognized text and full-text context for better semantic understanding. Utilizing the open-sourced ChFT dataset, we fine-tune a pre-trained LLM to evaluate CoC’s performance. Experiments show that CoC significantly outperforms baseline and benchmark systems in correcting full-text ASR outputs. We also analyze correction thresholds to balance under-correction and over-rephrasing, extrapolate CoC on extra-long ASR outputs, and explore using other types of information to guide error correction.

title: Clip-Driven Zero-Shot Learning with Ambiguous Labels
abstract: Zero-shot learning (ZSL) aims to recognize unseen classes by leveraging semantic information from seen classes, but most existing methods assume accurate class labels for training instances. However, in real-world scenarios, noise and ambiguous labels can significantly reduce the performance of ZSL. To address this, we propose a new CLIP-driven partial label zero-shot learning (CLIP-PZSL) framework to handle label ambiguity. First, we use CLIP to extract instance and label features. Then, a semantic mining block fuses these features to extract discriminative label embeddings. We also introduce a partial zero-shot loss, which assigns weights to candidate labels based on their relevance to the instance and aligns instance and label embeddings to minimize semantic mismatch. As the training goes on, the ground-truth labels are progressively identified, and the refined labels and label embeddings in turn help improve the semantic alignment of instance and label features. Comprehensive experiments on several datasets demonstrate the advantage of CLIP-PZSL.

title: CO-DRS: Data-Free Robustness Stealing Via Dual-Model Collaboration
abstract: Model stealing attacks threaten Machine Learning as a Service (MLaaS), where users access models via APIs without knowing their architecture or training data. Existing methods emphasize clean accuracy, while overlooking adversarial robustness. To address this, we propose a data-free dual-model robustness stealing (Co-DRS) that employs two surrogate models to achieve dual stealing of accuracy and robustness. The auxiliary surrogate learns robust behaviors via adversarial samples, while the primary surrogate leverages dual supervision from both the target and auxiliary models, trained on high-entropy samples. To accurately capture the decision boundary of the target model, a generator produces high-entropy samples, guided by diversity-promoting losses to prevent mode collapse. On CIFAR-10, the surrogate achieves 77.21% clean accuracy and 43.59% average robust accuracy, only 5.36% and 7.78% below the target model, respectively, outperforming existing baselines. Our work reveals robust models in MLaaS are highly vulnerable to this new dual-property theft, motivating new defense mechanisms.

title: Reward-Based Efficient Demonstration Selection for In-Context Learning
abstract: In-context learning (ICL) is a capability of Large Language Models (LLMs), but its performance is sensitive to the quality of in-context demonstrations. Existing demonstration selection methods either exhibit suboptimal performance due to rigid heuristics or incur prohibitive computational costs by relying on LLM-based scoring. To address these challenges, we propose REDS (Reward-Based Efficient Demonstration Selection), an effective and efficient framework for in-context demonstration selection. An innovation of REDS is the Efficient Annotator, an LLM-free module that constructs training data by annotating positive and negative examples based on output similarity, thereby obviating the need for costly LLM-based scoring. Furthermore, we introduce a reward model to select demonstrations by accurately evaluating the intricate relationship between queries and demonstrations. Validated through comprehensive experiments on diverse natural language processing (NLP) tasks, REDS achieves state-of-the-art performance while shedding new light on demonstration selection for ICL.

title: Subtractive Modulative Network with Learnable Periodic Activations
abstract: We propose the Subtractive Modulative Network (SMN), a novel, parameter-efficient Implicit Neural Representation (INR) architecture inspired by classical subtractive synthesis. The SMN is designed as a principled signal processing pipeline, featuring a learnable periodic activation layer (Oscillator) that generates a multi-frequency basis, and a series of modulative mask modules (Filters) that actively generate high-order harmonics. We provide both theoretical analysis and empirical validation for our design. Our SMN achieves a PSNR of 40+ dB on two image datasets, comparing favorably against state-of-the-art methods in terms of both reconstruction accuracy and parameter efficiency. Furthermore, consistent advantage is observed on the challenging 3D NeRF novel view synthesis task. Supplementary materials are available at https://inrainbws.github.io/smn/.

title: MAGE-KT: Multi-Agent Graph-Enhanced Knowledge Tracing with Subgraph Retrieval and Asymmetric Fusion
abstract: Knowledge Tracing (KT) aims to model a student’s learning trajectory and predict performance on the next question. A key challenge is how to better represent the relationships among students, questions, and knowledge concepts (KCs). Recently, graph-based KT paradigms have shown promise for this problem. However, existing methods have not sufficiently explored inter-concept relations, often inferred solely from interaction sequences. In addition, the scale and heterogeneity of KT graphs make full-graph encoding both computationally both costly and noise-prone, causing attention to bleed into student-irrelevant regions and degrading the fidelity of inter-KC relations. To address these issues, we propose a novel framework: Multi-Agent Graph-Enhanced Knowledge Tracing (MAGE-KT). It constructs a multi-view heterogeneous graph by combining a multi-agent KC relation extractor and a student–question interaction graph, capturing complementary semantic and behavioral signals. Conditioned on the target student’s history, it retrieves compact, high-value subgraphs and integrates them using an Asymmetric Cross-attention Fusion Module to enhance prediction while avoiding attention diffusion and irrelevant computation. Experiments on three widely used KT datasets show substantial improvements in KC-relation accuracy and clear gains in next-question prediction over existing methods.

title: Adding Compilation Metadata To Binaries To Make Disassembly Decidable
abstract: The binary executable format is the standard method for distributing and executing software. Yet, it is also as opaque a representation of software as can be. If the binary format were augmented with metadata that provides security-relevant information, such as which data is intended by the compiler to be executable instructions, or how memory regions are expected to be bounded, that would dramatically improve the safety and maintainability of software. In this paper, we propose a binary format that is a middle ground between a stripped black-box binary and open source. We provide a tool that generates metadata capturing the compiler's intent and inserts it into the binary. This metadata enables lifting to a correct and recompilable higher-level representation and makes analysis and instrumentation more reliable. Our evaluation shows that adding metadata does not affect runtime behavior or performance. Compared to DWARF, our metadata is roughly 17% of its size. We validate correctness by compiling a comprehensive set of real-world C and C++ binaries and demonstrating that they can be lifted, instrumented, and recompiled without altering their behavior.

title: Quantum Decoherence of the Surface Code: A Generalized Caldeira-Leggett Approach
abstract: Standard quantum error correction (QEC) models typically assume discrete, Markovian noise, obscuring the continuous quantum nature of physical environments. In this manuscript, we investigate the fundamental limits of an actively corrected surface code coupled to a continuous, un-reset quantum environment at zero and finite temperature. Using the generalized Caldeira-Leggett framework, we map the long-time evolution of the logical qubit to a boundary conformal field theory, establishing an exact equivalence to the anisotropic Kondo model. We evaluate computational times for a finite code distance $L$ for all spatial and temporal correlations. Our analysis reveals that a true thermodynamic threshold exists strictly for short-range environments ($z>1/(s+1)$). In critical or long-range regimes, the macroscopic footprint of the code weaponizes the continuous bath, hindering the topological protection.

title: Superficial Success vs. Internal Breakdown: An Empirical Study of Generalization in Adaptive Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: Adaptive multi-agent systems (MAS) are increasingly adopted to tackle complex problems. However, the narrow task coverage of their optimization raises the question of whether they can function as general-purpose systems. To address this gap, we conduct an extensive empirical study of adaptive MAS, revealing two key findings: (1) topological overfitting -- they fail to generalize across different domains; and (2) illusory coordination -- they achieve reasonable surface-level accuracy while the underlying agent interactions diverge from ideal MAS behavior, raising concerns about their practical utility. These findings highlight the pressing need to prioritize generalization in MAS development and motivate evaluation protocols that extend beyond simple final-answer correctness.

title: Distribution-Aware Mobility-Assisted Decentralized Federated Learning
abstract: Decentralized Federated Learning (DFL) eliminates reliance on a central server by enabling peer-to-peer model aggregation, but suffers from limited connectivity and non-IID data. In many applications, some clients are mobile, yet the role of mobility in DFL remains underexplored. This work shows that introducing even a small fraction of mobile clients, moving randomly, significantly improves information flow and accuracy. To further enhance performance, we propose structured distribution-aware mobility strategies, where mobile clients navigate the network using knowledge of data distributions and static client locations. These strategies mitigate the impact of data heterogeneity and accelerate convergence. Extensive experiments validate the effectiveness of induced mobility in DFL and demonstrate the superiority of our proposed mobility patterns over random movement.

title: Estimating the best separable approximation of non-pure spin-squeezed states
abstract: We discuss the estimation of the distance of a given mixed many-body quantum state to the set of fully separable states, applied to the concrete scenario of collective spin states. Concretely, we discuss lower bounds to distances from the set of fully separable states based on entanglement criteria and upper bounds to those distances using an iterative algorithm to find the optimal separable state closest to the target. Focusing on collective states of N spin- 1 / 2 particles, we consider spin-squeezing inequalities (SSIs), which provide a complete set of nonlinear entanglement criteria based on collective spin variances. First, we find a lower bound to distance-based entanglement monotones, specifically the so-called best separable approximation (BSA) from the complete set of SSIs, thereby bypassing entirely a numerical optimization over a (potentially very large) set of linear entanglement witnesses. Then, we improve current algorithms to iteratively find the closest separable state to a given target state, exploiting the symmetry of the system. These results allow us to study entanglement quantitatively on thermal states of spin systems on fully-connected graphs at nonzero temperature, as well as potentially similar states arising in out-of-equilibrium situations. We thus apply our methods to investigate entanglement across different phases of a fully-connected XXZ model. We observe that our lower bound becomes often tight for zero temperature as well as for the temperature at which entanglement disappears, both of which are thus precisely captured by the SSIs. We further observe, among other things, that entanglement can arise at nonzero temperature even in the ordered phase, where the ground state is separable, revealing the potential usefulness of entanglement quantification also beyond the ground state paradigm.

title: Hotelaria 4.0: Entre o Humano e o Algoritmo
abstract: Esta obra analisa a convergência entre a hospitalidade tradicional e as tecnologias disruptivas da Quarta Revolução Industrial. Através de uma abordagem transdisciplinar, o livro investiga o impacto da Inteligência Artificial (IA), da Automação de Processos (RPA) e da análise de dados na jornada do hóspede, propondo um modelo de gestão ciberfísico. O autor explora a superação da dicotomia entre eficiência tecnológica e calor humano, defendendo que a soberania digital e a ética no tratamento de dados são os novos pilares da lealdade na economia da experiência. Um guia essencial para compreender como a automação da logística operacional permite o resgate do papel do colaborador como anfitrião, priorizando o "toque humano" em um ecossistema crescentemente algorítmico.

title: AI-Enhanced CRM With Chatbots For Real Estate Lead Optimization
authors: Vaishnavi Mhaske, Aditya Shingane, Rohini Narwade, Sarthak Taru,Dipanjali Shipne
abstract: Customer Relationship Management (CRM) systems in the real estate sector often suffer from delayed response times and inefficient manual lead handling, leading to reduced conversion rates. This study examines the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based chatbots into CRM systems to address these limitations. A comprehensive review of existing literature and industry case studies indicates that AI chatbot adoption can improve lead conversion rates by up to 40%, reduce response time by 60%, and lower operational costs by 30–45%. A framework is proposed that incorporates Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques and Application Programming Interface (API) integration to enable automated and real-time customer interaction with synchronized data management. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed system can handle approximately 80–92% of customer queries, significantly enhancing user satisfaction and engagement. Additionally, empirical evidence from property management studies. supports the scalability and effectiveness of the approach in the Indian real estate context. The results suggest that AI-enabled CRM systems provide a scalable and efficient solution for improving customer engagement, optimizing lead management, and increasing overall business performance in the real estate domain.

title: Haiku Anagram Generation Using AI: Synthesising Poetic Isomers Through Metaphor-Driven Prompt Engineering (Educational Transformation 002)
abstract: Description (English) Overview This paper presents a novel approach to Japanese haiku anagram generation by extending a three-fold metaphorical framework—quantum mechanics, crystal-growth theory, and organic chemistry—to guide large language models (LLMs) in generating semantically independent new haikus from the identical 17 syllables (morae) of existing haikus. Key Findings: 1. Isomorphic Generation Success: We successfully demonstrate the generation of semantically and aesthetically independent alternative haikus from identical molecular formulae (17-syllable inventories), treating haiku syllables as organic isomers—compounds with identical atomic composition but radically different properties and meanings. 2. Discovery of Poetic Steganography: Haiku anagrams uniquely exhibit a "dual-plaintext structure," where both the original and generated haikus function as independently meaningful poems. This property—unknown in classical anagram theory—constitutes a new form of poetic steganography with high plausible deniability. 3. Metaphor-Driven Cognitive Amplification: By deliberately invoking organic chemistry terminology (structural isomers, enantiomers, racemic mixtures) in prompt design, we observe a quantifiable improvement in token efficiency and aesthetic coherence, demonstrating that humanistic metaphors can systematically redirect LLM outputs toward higher-order creative goals without algorithmic modification. Background & Context The author is a molecular biologist (specialising in RNA) developing liberal arts curricula for first-year undergraduates at the University of Tokyo. This research emerged not from AI expertise but from classroom practice—a workshop inspired by physicist Terahiko Terada's 1922 essay "Chawan no Yu" (A Lesson from a Tea Cup), which advocates connecting scientific and humanistic knowledge through metaphor. Previous work (Educational Transformation 001) applied quantum and crystallisation metaphors to English anagrams with success. However, when adapted to Japanese haikus, the dual-metaphor framework proved insufficient to capture haiku-specific constraints (5-7-5 syllable structure, kire or caesura, yohaku or poetic silence, seasonal reference). The addition of organic chemistry isomerism as a third metaphor resolved these limitations entirely. Methodological Innovation We introduce: - Three-tiered metaphor protocol: Quantum superposition (possibility-space management) → Crystal nucleation (hierarchical structure-building) → Isomeric transformation (semantic distance calibration) - Two-stage synthesis strategy: Molecular-level (preserving ligatures like chiyo as single morae) and thermal decomposition (atomic-level when molecular synthesis reaches impasse) - Five-axis aesthetic evaluation: Meaningfulness (0.30), kire (0.20), yohaku (0.20), tension with original (0.15), defamiliarisation (0.15) - Isomer taxonomy for poetry: 11 isomer-type classifications mapping to increasingly distant poetic transformations (from renzoku isomer to meso-structure) Practical Outcomes From a pedagogical standpoint, this framework enables students (regardless of domain expertise) to experience how metaphor functions as a cognitive technology—not merely literary decoration but a systematic tool for amplifying AI reasoning capacity. The protocol is fully reproducible and available as a prompt template compatible with any LLM. Broader Significance This work occupies the intersection of three disciplines: 1. Constrained literature (Oulipo aesthetics): How AI pursues poetic freedom within human-designed, absolute constraints (17 syllables) 2. Computational creativity: Using AI as a "mirror" that visualises the structure of human aesthetic intuition, rather than as an automated content generator 3. Prompt engineering as humanistic practice: Demonstrating that aesthetic goals can be achieved through metaphorical framing rather than technical modification 概要(日本語) 【授業実践】俳句をアナグラム処理して新しい俳句を作る生成AIワーク 西洋還元主義と美的感覚の協奏:Educational Transformation 002 要旨 本論は、既存の俳句の17音(モーラ)から、同一の音素組成を持ちながら意味として完全に独立した別の俳句を生成するために、量子力学・結晶成長論・有機化学という三重メタファーを大規模言語モデル(LLM)に適用するアプローチを提示する。 主要な発見: 1. 異性体としての句生成の成功:同一の分子式(17音の音素インベントリ)から、意味的・美的に独立した別句の生成に成功。俳句の音は「有機化学の異性体」と見立てることで、同一の原子組成を持ちながら全く異なる性質を示す化合物の概念を詩的に適用した。 2. 詩的ステガノグラフィの発見:俳句アナグラムは「二重平文構造」を持ち、元句も生成句も共に詩として完全に自立するという特性を示す。古典的なアナグラム理論では見られない現象で、「否認可能性」の極めて高い新しい詩的ステガノグラフィ形式を構成する。 3. メタファー駆動型認知増幅:有機化学用語(構造異性体、エナンチオマー、ラセミ体など)をプロンプトに明示的に導入することで、トークン消費量の劇的な改善と美的一貫性の向上を観察。アルゴリズム修正なしに、人文学的メタファーのみがLLMの創造的出力を高次目標へと体系的に誘導できることを実証した。 背景と文脈 著者は東京大学で教養教育の教材開発に携わる分子生物学(RNA専門)の教員であり、本研究はAI専門知ではなく授業実践から生まれた。物理学者・寺田寅彦の随筆「茶わんの湯」(1922)—科学と人文知をメタファーで繋ぐことを主張する古典的論考—を題材にした教養サロンのワークショップが起源である。 前稿(Educational Transformation 001)では量子力学メタファーと結晶成長論メタファーを英語アナグラムに適用して成功を収めた。しかし日本語俳句へ応用する際、この二重メタファーでは5-7-5という音数構造、「切れ」の機能、「余白」の価値、季語の扱いといった俳句固有の詩的制約を十分に捉えられないことが判明。有機化学の「異性体」概念を第三のメタファーとして追加することで、これら三点すべてが劇的に改善された。 方法論の革新性 本研究は以下を導入する: - title: K4Sekolah: School Context Data Files for TIMSS 2023 Grade 4
abstract: The official TIMSS 2023 website provides the School Context Data Files for TIMSS 2023 Grade 4 in rdata format. However, the available data are presented solely in the form of numerical values. This package aims to transform the numerical data into categorical data, thereby enabling clearer interpretation and reducing ambiguity in statistical data analysis. Furthermore, the category labels are presented in Bahasa Indonesia. This initiative is intended as a contribution to promoting and expanding the use of Bahasa Indonesia in the field of programming, in line with its designation as one of the official languages of the United Nations General Assembly.

title: Dynamic Learning in the Spatio-Temporal Continuum
abstract: While AI-driven clinical workflows in medical imaging offer significant potential for patient safety, model robustness and generalization are frequently hindered by the static world assumption of current AI models. In practice, this domain is highly dynamic, with distributions shifting significantly across both location (spatial) and time (temporal). For example, artifacts or changes in patient populations are inherent to medical imaging and manifest across both dimensions. Such diverse training data is usually not available from only one hospital or point in time. Since privacy regulations restrict the sharing of patient data between hospitals and its long-term storage, spatio-temporally distributed training is crucial to bridge the spatio-temporal data availability gap. Federated Learning and Continual Learning are well-established concepts to address these gaps. However, in the dynamic clinical reality, they suffer from performance degradation: Federated Learning is affected by Client Drift when data distributions differ spatially, while Continual Learning suffers from Catastrophic Forgetting when distributions shift over time. Existing methods address these separately or require prior knowledge of the underlying distribution changes. Consequently, existing research neglects the potential of a more dynamic joint method to robustly overcome data availability challenges in dynamic clinical environments. In the first part of this work, we empirically demonstrate a strong correlation between performance degradation caused by shifts in both dimensions, motivating the introduction of a new paradigm for robust spatio-temporally distributed training termed Dynamic Learning. We propose DynBC, a Dynamic Learning method that significantly outperforms existing conventional state-of-the-art approaches. Beyond the dynamic nature of medical imaging, the deployment of dynamic spatio-temporally distributed training to overcome the data availability gap is also hindered by rigid medical device regulations that fail to acknowledge the dynamic reality of medical imaging. We analyze the Predetermined Change Control Plan as a novel regulatory framework proposed by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration that is the first of its kind to address this issue from a regulatory perspective. We identify three critical gaps and propose solutions to each of them to fully enable the legal clinical deployment of dynamic models. Deploying spatio-temporally distributed training in real-world clinical settings is the last major challenge for our holistic approach to overcome the problem of data availability. Consequently, in this work, we present the first deployment of Federated Learning for histopathology segmentation of colorectal cancer tissue within the infrastructure of German university hospitals. In a nationwide project, we demonstrate the ability of our framework to train on data that is distributed across a geographic area of 10,500 km². By addressing these challenges, our work helps to bring these dynamic models closer to clinical reality. We bridge the gap between achieving robust training under spatio-temporal distribution shifts, regulatory adaptation, and translation into clinical applications, thereby improving clinical workflows and patient safety.

title: Shielding Federated Learning Services From a Novel Stealthy Label-Flipping Attack Exposing Membership
abstract: Label-flipping attacks pose a significant threat to the security and privacy of machine learning models, particularly in federated learning (FL). While existing defenses, such as FoolsGold and Krum, aim to mitigate these attacks, they often fail to account for more subtle adversarial behaviors, such as intermittent class-targeted flips. In this work, we introduce theStealthy Label-Flipping Attack (SLFA), which exposes this overlooked vulnerability in FL services. SLFA is an adaptive attack that intermittently flips a fixed subset of class labels across multiple communication rounds before reverting them to their original state. We show that this transient manipulation (i) evades state-of-the-art poisoning and anomaly detectors, (ii) preserves overall model utility, and (iii) introduces gradient instability during the attacking rounds, thereby increasing the risk of privacy leakage. To counter this hybrid threat that not only evades state-of-the-art defenses but also amplifies privacy leakage, we proposeFLStealthShield, a server-side defense mechanism that detects and neutralizes such adaptive attacks by analyzing temporal patterns in client updates. Extensive experiments under both IID and non-IID data distributions demonstrate that FLStealthShield achieves Byzantine robustness and maintains high model utility, outperforming existing defenses even when over 40% of clients are malicious.

We show that this transient manipulation (i) evades state-of-the-art poisoning and anomaly detectors, (ii) preserves overall model utility, and (iii) introduces gradient instability during the attacking rounds, thereby increasing the risk of privacy leakage. To counter this hybrid threat that not only evades state-of-the-art defenses but also amplifies privacy leakage, we proposeFLStealthShield, a server-side defense mechanism that detects and neutralizes such adaptive attacks by analyzing temporal patterns in client updates. Extensive experiments under both IID and non-IID data distributions demonstrate that FLStealthShield achieves Byzantine robustness and maintains high model utility, outperforming existing defenses even when over 40% of clients are malicious.

title: High-Speed Real-Time Random Bit Generation Based on a Modeless Raman Fiber Laser
abstract: True random numbers are essential for cryptography and secure communications. Algorithmically generated pseudo-random numbers lack true physical randomness, while conventional lasers as physical entropy sources introduce time-delay signatures (TDS) and require complex post processing. To address this challenge, this study presents a high speed, real-time true random bit generator utilizing a modeless Raman fiber laser (RFL). A modeless RFL was constructed using an ultra-low reflectivity (-27 dB) fiber Bragg grating (FBG) and a high-reflectivity FBG serving as cavity mirrors. The laser delivers stable modeless Raman lasing within the pump power range of 5 W to 10 W. Compared with multilongitudinal-mode operation, the modeless laser exhibits significantly lower temporal coherence. By truncating the four least significant bits of the 8-bit digitized temporal intensity signal from the modeless RFL, random bit sequences were generated at a rate of 320 Gbps. The resulting random bit stream shows a uniform distribution of bits 0 and 1, its autocorrelation function contains no TDS, and it successfully passes the NIST statistical test. In contrast, the same generation method fails to produce qualified random bits when applied to the Raman fiber laser operating in the multilongitudinal-mode regime. The demonstrated modeless RFL system combines real-time operation, high speed, and stability, offering a robust physical entropy source for cryptographic and secure communication applications.

title: Doctor Patient Summarizer: Transformer-based Patient-Friendly Medical Summaries
abstract: The conversations between patients and doctors include vital clinical data that should be properly recorded to enable effective clinical decision-making and patient comprehension. These interactions cannot be summarized in a manual manner that is both time-consuming and may cause inconsistencies, omissions and fatigue in documentation. Despite the recent advances in transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) models, which have enhanced automated clinical summarization models, a large number of the currently existing models have difficulties with the long conversational context and frequently give patients summaries that are hard to understand because of highly technical language. The present paper presents a proposal of a transformer-based system based on the Vision Transformer (ViT) architecture to produce concise, medically accurate and patient-friendly summaries of clinical conversations. The given strategy splits the dialogue tokens into regular semantic patches, which allows to generate a long context modeling efficiently and retain conversational coherence. The preprocessing pipeline including the speaker identification, medical terms normalization and the contextual filtering is added to enhance the factual consistency, and less ambiguity in the summaries generated. The model is trained on selected curated clinical dialogues datasets and compared with the standard summarization baselines with the help of classic metrics, such as ROUGE, BERT Score, and medical specificity accuracy indicators. Results of the experiment indicate that there is better summary coherence, factual preservation and readability than conventional transformer-based architectures. Also, attention-based interpretability indicates clinically significance of dialogue segments that are relevant towards the summary generation process. The suggested framework does not only lead to better clinical documentation efficiency and communication between the healthcare providers and the patients, but also aids in a safer and more transparent arrival of health care information.

title: Global Context-Aware Multi-Instance Learning for Whole Slide Image Classification
abstract: Multi-instance learning (MIL) is an effective weakly supervised learning paradigm where each sample is a bag of unlabeled instances, making it particularly suitable for whole slide image (WSI) classification, as WSIs can reach gigapixel resolutions, with supervision available only at the bag (WSI) level. However, WSIs often suffer from spurious correlations and an overwhelming number of negative instances, leading to underutilization of key instances. To address these issues, we propose the global context-aware multi-instance learning with asymmetric contrast (GCA-MIL) algorithm with two key strategies. The global context-aware (GCA) strategy consists of a class token, a global context, and a key instance, designed to extract and transfer contextual knowledge. Building on this, the asymmetric contrast strategy incorporates a triplet loss to strengthen the similarity between the global context and the key instance while reducing the association with negative anchor instances. Experiments on the CAMELYON16 dataset show that GCA-MIL outperforms state-of-the-art MIL approaches.

title: QCA-RAG: Efficient Retrieval for LLMs via Query Complexity Awareness
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has become a key paradigm for enhancing the knowledge and reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs). However, conventional approaches treat all queries uniformly, leading to unnecessary retrieval cost and suboptimal performance for queries of varying complexity. To adress thie issue, we propose QCA-RAG, a Query Complexity-Aware framework that dynamically adjusts retrieval behavior based on query complexity, enabling the LLM to generate high-quality responses with reduced retrieval overhead. Experiments on four datasets covering diverse query complexities show that QCA-RAG improves answer quality while reducing retrieval latency compared to both fixed and adaptive baselines, demonstrating its effectiveness in balancing efficiency and accuracy across factoid and multi-hop QA tasks.

title: Hybrid Continuous Variable Quantum Neural Network for Audio Classification
abstract: Audio classification is a key application in deep learning, and quantum machine learning (QML) provides new possibilities by capturing complex patterns in signals through parameterized quantum circuits. However, existing qubit-based models struggle to efficiently represent continuous-valued data common in audio processing, limiting their scalability and expressivity. Continuous Variable Quantum Computing (CVQC) offers a natural framework for processing real-valued data such as mel-spectrograms, addressing the limitations of qubit-based systems while introducing nonlinearity through non-gaussian gates to ensure universality. In CVQC, each qumode represents an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space, enabling compact yet expressive information representation. This work introduces a two-qumode Hybrid Continuous Variable Quantum Neural Network (HCVQNN) for audio classification that integrates classical neural layers with a CV quantum circuit for advanced feature extraction and encoding. Experiments conducted using PennyLane demonstrate that HCVQNN achieves comparable audio classification accuracy while requiring fewer resources compared to classical deep networks and qubit-based quantum models.

title: Ara-BEST-RQ: Multi Dialectal Arabic SSL
abstract: We present Ara-BEST-RQ, a family of self-supervised learning (SSL) models specifically designed for multi-dialectal Arabic speech processing. Leveraging 5,640 hours of crawled Creative Commons speech and combining it with publicly available datasets, we pre-train conformer-based BEST-RQ models up to 600M parameters. Our models are evaluated on dialect identification (DID) and automatic speech recognition (ASR) tasks, achieving state-of-the-art performance on the former while using fewer parameters than competing models. We demonstrate that family-targeted pre-training on Arabic dialects significantly improves downstream performance compared to multilingual or monolingual models trained on non-Arabic data. All models, code, and pre-processed datasets will be publicly released to support reproducibility and further research in Arabic speech technologies.

title: AngularDINO: Semi-Supervised Anomaly Detection via Self-Distillation with Hybrid Angular Margin
abstract: Anomaly detection often suffers when training data assumed to be normal are contaminated with anomalies, causing severe performance degradation. Semi-supervised approaches attempt to leverage a few labeled anomalies, but they remain fragile to contamination and can even perform worse than unsupervised methods. To address this issue, we propose AngularDINO, a novel self-distillation framework that incorporates a key mechanism, called the hybrid angular margin. This mechanism applies complementary margins to the student and teacher networks: an additive margin encourages the student to form a discriminative feature space, while a subtractive margin ensures the teacher provides stable supervision. Through this design, AngularDINO enables robust anomaly detection even with limited labeled data. Experiments on standard benchmarks demonstrate that AngularDINO achieves significant performance gains over previous unsupervised and semi-supervised methods under contaminated scenarios.

title: QPath: A Question-Aware Multi-Resolution Vision Language Framework for Computational Pathology
abstract: Computational pathology has recently advanced through the use of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) for visual question answering (VQA). However, most existing approaches rely on single-resolution analysis of pathology images, limiting their ability to capture both global and fine-grained morphological cues. In this work, we introduce QPath, a novel MLLM that integrates multi-resolution analysis via question-aware patch retrieval. For region-of-interest (ROI) images, QPath crops them into patches and fuses the top-k question-relevant patches with the original view to enhance localized reasoning. For whole-slide images (WSIs), we propose a dynamic sampling strategy that balances spatial coverage with semantic relevance, enabling efficient yet comprehensive slide-level understanding. Extensive experiments show that QPath achieves state-of-the-art performance on ROI-level VQA benchmarks and exhibits strong zero-shot generalization to WSI-level tasks.

title: Improving Automatic Speech Recognition by Mitigating Distortions Introduced by Speech Enhancement Under Drone Noise
abstract: This paper proposes a method to improve automatic speech recognition (ASR) performance against drone noise-contaminated audio recordings by mitigating distortions resulted from speech enhancement (SE). Our system combines a front-end Adaptive Fusion Model (AFM) with a back-end Biasing Network (BN). The AFM, serving as the core of our proposed fusion-based method, adaptively fuses intermediate outputs from a diffusion-based SE model to optimize the noise-distortion trade-off, while the BN mitigates acoustic mismatch by correcting speech features using static noise characteristics, thereby avoiding costly ASR retraining. Experimental results with three types of drone noise across multiple signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) levels (0, -5, and -10 dB) demonstrated the robustness of the proposed system. In particular, for SNRs of -5 dB and above, the method consistently showed clear effectiveness, yielding about 20- and 25-point absolute character error rate (CER) improvements at 0 and -5 dB, respectively, compared to an ASR-only baseline.

title: Role-Specialist and Confidence-Selective Multi-Teacher Collaborative Distillation for Multi-Source Domain Adaptation
abstract: Multi-source domain adaptation is hampered by compounded inter-domain gaps and scarce target labels, making it hard for a single model to disentangle invariant from specific features. To address this, we propose a multi-teacher collaborative distillation framework that assigns distinct roles to different teachers: multi-source teachers focus on distilling robust domain-invariant knowledge, while a target-domain teacher leverages the collective wisdom of the source teachers to generate reliable pseudo-labels and capture the unique distribution of the target domain. These teachers interact via mutual distillation to dynamically integrate domain-invariant and domain-specific knowledge. Further, to meet resource constraints, a lightweight student model is introduced, which first absorbs global knowledge via standard distillation and then refines high-confidence target samples through disentangled knowledge distillation. This yields representations that are both generalizable and precise. Extensive experiments on standard image classification benchmarks demonstrate significant improvements over existing methods.

title: Optimized cross-attention GRU-transformer network with sooty tern algorithm for accurate solar power forecasting
abstract: Accurate forecasting of solar Photovoltaic (PV) power remains challenging due to data uncertainty, environmental fluctuations, and missing sensor values. To address these issues, this study introduces, an integrated deep learning and optimization framework designed for real-time PV power prediction. The approach begins with a rigorous data preprocessing pipeline that incorporates a hybrid imputation strategy combining Simple Imputer for categorical gaps and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) imputer for numerical inconsistencies. Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) and time-series decomposition further enhance the temporal interpretability of the dataset, while engineered feature transformations provide more informative inputs. The proposed hybrid STO-CrossEchoTransGRUNet model fuses the strengths of an Echo State Network (ESN) for global temporal encoding, a cross-attention transformer (CATL) for modelling multi-feature interactions and a Bidirectional GRU for capturing long-term bidirectional dependencies. To further boost performance, hyperparameters are optimized using Sooty Tern Optimization (STO) with a Levy flight–based spiral foraging mechanism. Benchmarking against traditional machine learning models and contemporary deep learning architectures demonstrates the superior accuracy, robustness and computational efficiency of the proposed method. Experimental evaluation validates significant improvements, achieving aRoot Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.015, Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.005, Median Absolute Error (MedAE) of 0.002, R² of 0.995 and consistently stable performance across varying environmental conditions. These results highlight STO-CrossEchoTransGRUNet as a highly reliable and scalable solution for real-time solar PV forecasting.

title: FG$^2$-GDN: Enhancing Long-Context Gated Delta Networks with Doubly Fine-Grained Control
abstract: Linear attention mechanisms have emerged as promising alternatives to softmax attention, offering linear-time complexity during inference. Recent advances such as Gated DeltaNet (GDN) and Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) have demonstrated that the delta rule, an online gradient descent update, enables superior associative recall compared to simple additive updates. While KDA refined the coarse head-wise decay gate into channel-wise decay, the learning rate $β_t$ in the delta update remains a scalar, limiting the model's capacity for dimension-specific adaptation. We introduce FG$^2$-GDN, which replaces the scalar $β_t$ with a channel-wise vector analogous to the transition from SGD to per-coordinate adaptive optimizers such as AdaGrad and Adam. We further propose FG$^2$-GDN+, which decouples the scaling for keys and values, enabling independent control of erasure strength and write strength. Experiments on synthetic and real-world benchmarks show that FG$^2$-GDN and its variant improve associative recall and long-context understanding over GDN and KDA, with comparable computational efficiency.

title: AutomationBench
abstract: Existing AI benchmarks for software automation rarely combine cross-application coordination, autonomous API discovery, and policy adherence. Real business workflows demand all three: a single task may span a CRM, inbox, calendar, and messaging platform - requiring the agent to find the right endpoints, follow a policy document, and write correct data to each system. To address this gap, we introduce AutomationBench, a benchmark for evaluating AI agents on cross-application workflow orchestration via REST APIs. Drawing on real workflow patterns from Zapier's platform, tasks span Sales, Marketing, Operations, Support, Finance, and HR domains. Agents must discover relevant endpoints themselves, follow layered business rules, and navigate environments with irrelevant and sometimes misleading records. Grading is programmatic and end-state only: whether the correct data ended up in the right systems. Even the best frontier models currently score below 10%. AutomationBench provides a challenging, realistic measure of where current models stand relative to the agentic capabilities businesses actually need.

title: ISSE: An Instruction-Guided Speech Style Editing Dataset and Benchmark
abstract: Speech style editing refers to modifying the stylistic properties of speech while preserving its linguistic content and speaker identity. However, most existing approaches depend on explicit labels or reference audio, which limits both flexibility and scalability. More recent attempts to use natural language descriptions remain constrained by oversimplified instructions and coarse style control. To address these limitations, we introduce an Instruction-guided Speech Style Editing Dataset (ISSE). The dataset comprises nearly 400 hours of speech and over 100,000 source-target pairs, each aligned with diverse and detailed textual editing instructions. We also build a systematic instructed speech data generation pipeline leveraging large language model, expressive text-to-speech and voice conversion technologies to construct high-quality paired samples. Furthermore, we train an instruction-guided autoregressive speech model on ISSE and evaluate it in terms of instruction adherence, timbre preservation, and content consistency. Experimental results demonstrate that ISSE enables accurate, controllable, and generalizable speech style editing compared to other datasets. The project page of ISSE is available at https://ychenn1.github.io/ISSE/.

title: RetrieveAll: A Multilingual Named Entity Recognition Framework with Large Language Models
abstract: The rise of large language models has led to breakthroughs in named entity recognition for high-resource languages, yet substantial room for improvement remains in low- and medium-resource languages. Existing multilingual named entity recognition methods face severe language interference during the multi-language adaptation process, manifested in feature conflicts between different languages and the competitive suppression of low-resource language features by high-resource languages. Although training a dedicated model for each language can mitigate such interference, it lacks scalability and incurs excessive computational costs in real-world applications. To address this issue, we propose RetrieveAll, a universal multilingual named entity recognition framework based on dynamic LoRA. The framework decouples task-specific features across languages and demonstrates efficient dynamic adaptability. Furthermore, we introduce a cross-granularity knowledge augmented method that fully exploits the intrinsic potential of the data without relying on external resources. Experimental results show that RetrieveAll achieves an average F1 improvement of 12.1% on the PAN-X dataset.

Although training a dedicated model for each language can mitigate such interference, it lacks scalability and incurs excessive computational costs in real-world applications. To address this issue, we propose RetrieveAll, a universal multilingual named entity recognition framework based on dynamic LoRA. The framework decouples task-specific features across languages and demonstrates efficient dynamic adaptability. Furthermore, we introduce a cross-granularity knowledge augmented method that fully exploits the intrinsic potential of the data without relying on external resources. Experimental results show that RetrieveAll achieves an average F1 improvement of 12.1% on the PAN-X dataset.

title: TestAgent: Automatic Benchmarking and Exploratory Interaction for Evaluating LLMS in Vertical Domains
abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in highly specialized vertical domains, the evaluation of their domain-specific performance becomes critical. However, existing evaluations for vertical domains typically rely on the labor-intensive construction of static single-turn datasets, which present two key limitations: (i) manual data construction is costly and must be repeated for each new domain, and (ii) static single-turn evaluations are misaligned with the dynamic multi-turn interactions in real-world applications, limiting the assessment of professionalism and stability. To address these, we propose TestAgent, a framework for automatic benchmarking and exploratory dynamic evaluation in vertical domains. TestAgent leverages retrieval-augmented generation to create domain-specific questions from user-provided knowledge sources, combined with a two-stage criteria generation process, thereby enabling scalable and automated benchmark creation. Furthermore, it introduces a reinforcement learning-guided multi-turn interaction strategy that adaptively determines question types based on real-time model responses, dynamically probing knowledge boundaries and stability. Extensive experiments across medical, legal, and governmental domains demonstrate that TestAgent enables efficient cross-domain benchmark generation and yields deeper insights into model behavior through dynamic exploratory evaluation. This work establishes a new paradigm for automated and in-depth evaluation of LLMs in vertical domains.

title: Integrating AI to Improve Customer Experience and Marketing in Zambia’s Insurance Sector: A Case Study of Selected Insurance Firms
abstract: The rapid evolution of digital technologies has significantly transformed service delivery and customer engagement in the global insurance industry. Artificial Intelligence (AI) plays a central role in this transformation by enhancing operational efficiency, personalizing customer interactions, and improving marketing strategies. However, the adoption and impact of AI in Zambia’s insurance sector remain limited and underexplored. This study investigates the integration of AI to improve customer experience and marketing effectiveness in selected Zambian insurance firms using a mixed-methods approach. Quantitative data from 100 respondents revealed that 63% reported some use of AI systems, while only 31% confirmed the presence of AI chatbots. Mean scores for AI usage and marketing effectiveness were 3.21 and 3.22, with a moderate positive correlation (r = 0.566, p < 0.01). Qualitative findings from 25 interviews highlighted key themes, including limited enterprise-level adoption, operational efficiency gains, improved customer targeting, and reliance on hybrid service models. Barriers such as skills gaps, data limitations, and unclear regulations persist. The study concludes that while AI offers significant opportunities, its full potential depends on strategic implementation, capacity building, and regulatory support within Zambia’s insurance sector.

title: Enhancing Arabic NLP
abstract: Arabic is a first language for more than 300 million people. It has some unique features that can make it one of the most complex languages, such as multiple derivatives, unlimited vocabulary, diacritics, and others. Preprocessing Arabic text is an essential step in order to prepare text for Natural Language Processing (NLP) purposes. This article provides a comparison study of several preprocessing tools for Arabic text. It explains the challenges in pre-processing the Arabic language as well as the techniques that used in every particular tool. However, the authors used the PRISMA for reporting the systematic reviews, which they started with screening 200 articles and ended-up with including only 30 articles. After reviewing these articles deeply, the results show that different tools such as AMIRA, CAMel ,and NLP packages added value in text-preprocessing. However, most of this papers considered that the ambiguity in Arabic orthography as well as the dialectal variants are the most challenges in Arabic NLP.

title: Multimodal Deep Learning-based Precision Treatment for Lung Cancer
abstract: Early and accurate classification of lung cancer is important in the development of an effective treatment plan and the achievement of high survival rates. This paper presents the development of a multimodal deep learning framework for the classification of lung cancer based on the use of computed tomography imaging and clinical data. ROI images of the tumor-focused CT scans are used in the imaging analysis process. The clinical features were preprocessed using encoding and normalization, while fully connected neural networks were used in the modeling process. Feature-level fusion is also used in the study, which is done by concatenating the features in the proposed framework. Five-fold cross-validation is used in the study. Pre-trained convolutional neural networks, including VGG16, ResNet50, DenseNet121, and EfficientNetB0, were used in the study to explore the use of the networks in the automated feature extraction process from the CT scans. The proposed model shows better performance compared to other existing techniques.

title: DSG: Dual-Semantic Guidance from LLM to Token Distillation for Few-Shot Incremental Learning
abstract: Few-shot class-incremental learning (FSCIL) must acquire new classes from limited data while preserving prior knowledge, where overfitting and catastrophic forgetting remain key challenges. Prior work typically relies on a single semantic cue, such as class names or descriptions, to complement visual features. We propose DSG, a dual-semantic guidance framework that distills complementary textual semantics into the ViT language branch without modifying the visual backbone: (i) TLTA, a template-driven low-rank text adapter that maps fixed-format class names to a session-stable semantic anchor; and (ii) DG-TSA, a description-guided, temperature-scaled attention that aggregates attribute-grouped descriptions into a dynamic semantic prototype. Together, DSG provides stable anchors to suppress semantic drift and adaptive fine-grained cues beyond static prompts, improving novel-class adaptation while retaining old knowledge. Experiments on CUB-200, miniImageNet, and CIFAR-100 demonstrate consistent gains over strong baselines. Code is available at: https://github.com/BUCT-IUSRC/Research__DSG.

title: Adaptive Defense Against Stationary Test-Time Attacks on Classifiers
abstract: In many classification tasks performed by autonomous systems, a classifier model is continuously used to compute decisions for a series of incoming test examples. In such scenarios, a test-time attack may falsify a series of test examples to continuously perturb the classification decisions of the system. Under the assumption of time-invariant but unknown attack mapping, we propose a novel adaptive defense approach consisting of two main components: an attack-type detector that identifies the nature of the ongoing attack from a small batch of attacked examples, and a set of specialized expert classifiers, each adversarially trained to be robust against a specific attack type. At test-time, the detector routes the input batch to the appropriate expert classifier. We demonstrate through experiments on the CIFAR-10 dataset that our adaptive defense significantly outperforms static defense approaches, highlighting the benefits of adapting the classifier model by leveraging the inferred characteristics of the ongoing attack.

title: DynaPredict: Alternating Predictive and Real Iteration for Efficient Deep Reinforcement Learning Training
abstract: Sample-inefficient in Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) impedes scalability and practical deployment. While model-based Reinforcement Learning (MBRL) improves efficiency through environmental simulation, it suffers from model bias and high computational costs. Conversely, conventional optimizers adapt poorly to DRL’s non-stationary optimization landscapes. To bridge this gap, we introduce DynaPredict, a novel optimization framework that transposes the concept of environmental simulation from observation space to parameter space. Instead of predicting observations, DynaPredict employs a lightweight predictive component to forecast the trajectory of policy parameter updates, thereby implicitly encoding environmental feedback. Our method alternates between predictive and real update cycles, drastically reducing environment interactions while avoiding model bias. Empirically, DynaPredict achieves consistent performance gains across the Atari benchmark, reducing sample complexity by up to 60% and accelerating wall-clock convergence time, demonstrating benefits orthogonal to specific algorithms or parallel architectures.

title: TAML: Task-Aware Metric-Driven Meta Learning for Few-Shot Action Recognition
abstract: Recent few-shot action recognition (FSAR) methods often adopt pre-trained visual backbones with temporal alignment modules for metric-based classification. However, directly fine-tuning large models or inserting lightweight adapters without explicit guidance fails to emphasize task-relevant metric representations. With limited samples and high-capacity backbones, adapting these models to learn transferable metric features remains challenging. To address this, we propose TAML, a task-level meta-learning paradigm that constructs meta-metric tasks to explicitly learn metric-relevant representations and enhance generalization. Our framework integrates task-specific learning, where the model captures metric information for individual tasks, with task-agnostic learning, which optimizes shared meta-features to capture multi-grained matching information. Experiments on standard datasets show that TAML consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods.

title: Palette: A Background-Robust Fingerprinting Attack on Air Interface Designed for Cross-Environment Challenges
abstract: Smartphones are indispensable devices in daily life. Due to the openness of the air interface between user equipment (UE) and base station (BS), wireless fingerprint sniffing has emerged as a significant privacy threat. Previous studies have conducted attacks in laboratory environments, assuming no background apps are running on the target UEs. This idealistic assumption diminishes the practicality of air interface fingerprint attacks. In this paper, we propose Palette, a novel fingerprint attack adaptable to various background environments. Specifically, Palette employs a pre-built background traffic library to augment the raw data. Subsequently, Palette utilizes multi-level traffic aggregation to extract robust features from the augmented traffic. Finally, drawing inspiration from speaker recognition, Palette builds a robust classifier based on Time Delay Neural Network (TDNN). Extensive cross-environment experiments demonstrate that Palette outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods and improves the F1-score for app identification by an average of 28.01% when other background applications are running.
